FliEdit: four calls for you

The HyperFrames gap work runs in two lanes. Lane A builds the obvious items on its own, one at a time. Lane B is this page: the items that need your taste or a ruling. Nothing here gets built until you answer, and nothing waits on it.

Lane A · building without you, in order
  1. Shortcuts popover from the key list (U6)
  2. Snap / link state at the timeline (U5)
  3. Track collapse + height (U7)
  4. Loop + fullscreen on the transport (U4)
  5. Inspector header + empty state (U3)
  6. Music duck verb with volume points (H1)
  7. Thumbnails + waveforms in clips (U2)
  8. Export audit (H4)
Lane B · your four calls, below
  1. The whole look: go light? (U1, U8)
  2. Keyframes: how much motion? (H2)
  3. On-screen text: who owns it? (H3)
  4. Speed change: un-defer? (H5)

Not now: "ask agent about this element" (U9, belongs to element chat); motion polish (U10).

01

U1 + U8 · The whole look: light, quiet chrome

Look and feel

HyperFrames Studio is cream and white panels, soft borders, small calm type, one accent. FliEdit has a dark timeline and dark panels with a brown/cream inspector and big type. U8 (tinting the selected clip's whole lane) is the same kind of call.

DecisionShould FliEdit go light (cream page, white panels, hairlines, brown text, yellow only for Export), the way FliStudio already looks?
My recommendationYes, go light, as one Lane A job afterwards: AppyDave is a light-only brand and FliStudio is already there. Keep FliEdit's layout; change only the surfaces, type sizes and borders. Fold U8's lane tint in.
02

H2 · Keyframes (move, scale, fade over time)

Product direction

HyperFrames animates anything over time with keyframe diamonds in the timeline. FliEdit's clip properties are fixed for the whole clip.

DecisionDoes FliEdit own motion (keyframes on clips), or does motion stay HyperFrames' job, with FliEdit the assembler?
My recommendationSmall yes: build one envelope model for volume first (H1, already Lane A), then reuse it for opacity and position only. No easing curves, no motion design: anything richer goes to HyperFrames.
03

H3 · Text and graphics on screen (callouts, burned-in captions)

Product direction

HyperFrames draws callouts as HTML and renders them into the video. FliEdit has no text layer: overlays are images or alpha video made elsewhere, and captions can only be soft subtitles (gap G5). Overlay Pilot already makes text overlays for Joy's videos.

DecisionWho owns on-screen text: FliEdit (a text clip), Overlay Pilot (makes the overlays FliEdit places), or HyperFrames (the motion layer)?
My recommendationOverlay Pilot makes it, FliEdit places it. FliEdit gets one small text clip only for burned-in captions (fixes G5). Designed callouts stay in Overlay Pilot / HyperFrames, so there's one place that knows your brand styling.
04

H5 · Speed change (slow-mo, fast-forward clips)

Ruling (was deferred)

FliEdit's gap ledger lists speed changes as intentionally deferred: named in B590 and never discussed. HyperFrames accepts a rate on clips.

DecisionUn-defer speed change for FliEdit?
My recommendationYes, later in Lane A (after A8): it's a clear verb (clip.setProps {speed}) and testable, but it touches ripple and audio pitch, so it goes after the duck work settles.
